correctness.rationale: Finite Esakia duality is specialized to a pointwise equality; a direct implication counterexample establishes its necessity. A descending recurrence counts every bounded morphism by its exact image using Stirling surjections. In constant width m>=2, only full-target frontiers enable more levels, singleton frontiers force collapse and the bottom level is unrestricted. Enumeration and image-upset cardinalities yield the polynomial for every m>=2 and h>=1. A standalone verifier independently checked 52,165 maps over 31 finite weak orders, plus 36 further uniform recurrence cases and 319 direct Heyting implication comparisons. Limits: finite checking is corroborative only; correctness rests on the algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: This is a complete implication-preserving endomorphism classification and rank-generating polynomial for natural equal-width weak-order Esakia posets, plus a nonuniform image-set recurrence. General Esakia duality and weak-order monotone-map counts predate the work. The closest full-text published weak-order mapping-space recurrence counts all monotone maps, which need not preserve Heyting implication and has no analogous endomorphism-rank polynomial. The inspected retraction theorem classifies ordinary order-preserving retracts, not all implication-preserving homomorphisms. The source literature did not reveal coverage; older unindexed equivalences remain a risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent count may occur in older or unindexed literature under terminology such as p-morphism monoids, finite Esakia endomorphism types or weak-order implication algebras.
No independent originality assessment has been performed; record-based searches are not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Finite weak orders are a natural height-width family for finite Esakia duality. The difference between continuous and implication-preserving self-maps is substantive and previously unclear from the inspected published all-map recurrences. This produces a complete structural classification and exact image-rank multiplicities in every uniform dimension, not an isolated small numerical example, and an exact nonuniform extension. The result is useful for homomorphism/image and finite implication-algebra studies without requiring a downstream universal theorem.
